summary: AI observability tools provide visibility into how LLM applications behave in production by tracing requests, evaluating output quality, and tracking token usage and spend. As LLM-powered features scale, these tools become essential for controlling costs, debugging complex agent workflows, and ensuring reliability and quality. Choosing the right platform depends on whether your priority is deep evaluation, cost gatekeeping, or end-to-end monitoring.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: End-to-end traces, LLM/chain/agent executions, latency, token usage, cost, and evaluation metrics, with deep integration into the LangChain ecosystem.
features: Detailed request tracing and debugging of chains and agents
Native LangChain and LangGraph integration (framework-agnostic SDK also available)
tools.pricing: Free tier limited to ~5,000 monthly traces; Plus/paid plans scale per trace. Analyses in 2026 estimate trace costs at roughly 5-10% of underlying LLM API spend for trace-heavy workloads.
tools.best_for: Teams building on LangChain/LangGraph that need rich tracing plus built-in evaluation and prompt iteration.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: API requests through a proxy/gateway, metering request volume, token usage, latency, and computed per-request cost across models.
features: Gateway/proxy-based request metering with minimal code changes
Caching and rate limiting to reduce spend
Request logging, dashboards, and user-level analytics
tools.pricing: Free up to 10,000 requests/traces per month; paid usage around $79 per 100,000 traces.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting a lightweight gateway for fast cost tracking, caching, and request-level analytics with minimal integration effort.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B)
tools.monitors: The full ML/LLM lifecycle including experiments, model training, fine-tuning runs, and LLM traces/evaluations via W&B Weave.
features: W&B Weave for LLM tracing and evaluation
tools.pricing: Free tier for individuals/personal projects; usage-based Pro and custom Enterprise plans for teams.
tools.best_for: ML teams that need unified observability across traditional model training, fine-tuning, and LLM application tracing.

tools.name: Arize AI
tools.monitors: Production model and LLM performance, including drift, data quality, embeddings, token usage, cost, and quality evaluations; open-source Arize Phoenix for tracing.
features: ML and LLM observability with drift and performance monitoring
Arize Phoenix open-source tracing and evaluation
tools.pricing: Free open-source Phoenix; free tier for Arize cloud with usage-based Pro and custom Enterprise pricing.
tools.best_for: Enterprises needing production-grade monitoring, drift detection, and RAG/embedding analysis at scale.

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: LLM application traces, nested spans, token usage, cost, latency, evaluation scores, and user feedback, with strong open-source/self-hosting support.
features: Nested trace and span visualization for agents
Cost and token tracking per trace
Evaluations, scoring, and user feedback collection
tools.pricing: Free and open-source (self-hosted); managed cloud offers a free Hobby tier plus usage-based Pro and Enterprise plans.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting an open-source, self-hostable observability stack with flexible tracing and cost tracking.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM calls, vector DB queries, and framework operations via OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation, capturing traces, latency, token usage, and cost.
features: Auto-instrumentation for popular LLM SDKs and frameworks
Vendor-neutral export to any OTel-compatible backend
Traces for vector databases and RAG pipelines
tools.pricing: Free and open-source; optional Traceloop managed backend with free and paid usage-based tiers.
tools.best_for: Teams standardizing on OpenTelemetry who want vendor-neutral instrumentation exportable to existing observability backends.

cost_tips: Use smaller or cheaper models for simpler tasks and reserve frontier models for complex reasoning, routing requests by difficulty.
Implement prompt and response caching for repeated or similar queries to avoid redundant paid API calls.
Optimize prompts and trim context: shorten system prompts, limit retrieved context, and cap max output tokens to reduce token spend.
Set budgets, rate limits, and alerts using a gateway or observability tool to catch runaway costs and monitor spend per feature or user.
